entities.name: Paracoccidioidomycosis
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous systemic fungal infection caused by dimorphic fungi of the Paracoccidioides genus, endemic to Latin America, presenting as either an acute juvenile form with reticuloendothelial dissemination or a chronic adult form with moriform stomatitis, pulmonary butterfly-wing infiltrates, and adrenal involvement.

entities.name: Inhalation of Aerosolized Microconidia from Disturbed Acidic Soil in Latin America
entities.description: Inhalation of airborne infectious microconidia released into aerosols from disturbed acidic, humid topsoil during rural environmental activities in continental Latin America.

entities.name: Rural Agricultural Worker in South America Coffee and Tobacco Plantations
entities.description: Occupational rural labor involving manual manipulation of soil and crops (coffee harvesting, tobacco farming, earth moving, tilling) in hyperendemic South American regions, especially Brazil, Colombia, and Venezuela.

entities.name: Sylvatic Animal Reservoir Contact with Nine-Banded Armadillos and Rural Canines
entities.description: Environmental cohabitation or direct contact with natural animal reservoirs including nine-banded armadillos (Dasypus novemcinctus) and rural domestic dogs harboring Paracoccidioides in endemic areas.

entities.name: Male Agricultural Smoker with Chronic Alcohol Consumption Lifestyle
entities.description: Demographic and behavioral profile of adult males (10:1 to 15:1 male-to-female ratio) with history of heavy tobacco smoking (>14-fold elevated risk) and regular distilled alcohol intake exceeding 50 g/day.

entities.name: Absence of Inhibitory Circulating 17-Beta-Estradiol Protection in Adult Males
entities.description: Lack of female 17-beta-estradiol hormone, which normally binds fungal cytoplasmic estrogen receptors and blocks mycelium-to-yeast dimorphic transformation, allowing unchecked yeast conversion in adult males.

entities.name: Prolonged Decade-Scale Clinical Latency Following Remote Latin American Residence
entities.description: Remote residential or travel history in Latin America with dormant quiescent fungal foci undergoing clinical reactivation 10 to 30 or more years after emigrating from the endemic zone.

entities.name: Paracoccidioides brasiliensis
entities.description: Thermally dimorphic fungal pathogen belonging to the Ajellomycetaceae family, existing as infective mycelia/microconidia at 20-25°C and transforming into large, multi-budding thick-walled parasitic yeast cells at 37°C.

entities.name: Paracoccidioides lutzii
entities.description: Distinct cryptic species within the Paracoccidioides genus predominantly localized to the Center-West and Amazon basin of Brazil, causing endemic systemic paracoccidioidomycosis.

entities.name: Moriform Painful Stomatitis with Mulberry-Like Granulomatous Gingival Ulcers
entities.description: Painful, granular, infiltrative mucosal ulcerations studded with pinpoint red hemorrhagic spots (mulberry-like stomatitis of Aguiar-Pupo) affecting lips, gums, tongue, and palate, accompanied by intense odynophagia, sialorrhea, loose teeth, and cervical lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Acute Juvenile Fulminant Reticuloendothelial Dissemination with Suppurative Fistulizing Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Rapidly progressive disease in children and young adults under 30 years of age with massive peripheral and intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy that softens and ulcerates with draining fistulae, profound hepatosplenomegaly, and osteolytic bone lesions without prominent lung involvement.

entities.name: Bilateral Adrenal Granulomatous Destruction with Primary Addisonian Adrenal Insufficiency
entities.description: Granulomatous infiltration and necrotizing destruction of adrenal cortices in chronic disease manifesting as profound asthenia, postural hypotension, cutaneous melanoderma, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia.

entities.name: Chronic Progressive Fibrosing Pulmonary Syndrome with Exertional Dyspnea and Cor Pulmonale
entities.description: Chronic productive cough, mucopurulent sputum, hemoptysis, and progressive dyspnea resulting from extensive peribronchovascular and interstitial pulmonary fibrosis leading to pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale.

entities.name: Microscopic Mariner Wheel or Pilot Wheel Multi-Budding Yeast on Direct KOH Preparation
entities.description: Direct microscopic examination (10-20% KOH mount or calcofluor white) of mucosal scrapings, sputum, or lymph node aspirates revealing large spherical mother yeast cells (15-30 μm up to 60 μm) surrounded by multiple narrow-necked daughter blastoconidia (rueda de timón / pilot wheel or Mickey Mouse appearance).

entities.name: Bilateral Symmetrical Butterfly-Wing Infiltrates Spared at Apices and Bases on Chest Imaging
entities.description: Chest radiography or CT demonstrating bilateral, symmetrical coarse reticulonodular opacities and alveolar consolidations concentrated in perihilar and mid-lung zones (butterfly-wing or bat-wing pattern), with characteristic sparing of the lung apices and bases, reversed halo signs, and interlobular septal thickening.

entities.name: High-Resolution CT Reversed Halo Sign with Perihilar Nodular Ground-Glass Opacities
entities.description: High-resolution computed tomography finding of the reversed halo sign (central ground-glass opacity encircled by a crescentic or complete ring of consolidation) alongside centrolobular nodules and interlobular septal thickening.

entities.name: Marked Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia Exceeding 10 to 30 Percent in Juvenile Presentation
entities.description: Marked elevation of absolute peripheral blood eosinophil count (frequently 10-30% or more) on admission CBC, highly characteristic of the acute/subacute juvenile form, accompanied by elevated ESR and CRP.

entities.name: Positive Serum Double Immunodiffusion Precipitin Band Against gp43 Antigen
entities.description: Quantitative serum double immunodiffusion (DID) demonstrating diagnostic precipitin bands against the 43-kDa glycoprotein (gp43) of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis with >90% sensitivity and >95% specificity.

entities.name: Serum Electrolyte Pattern of Addisonian Adrenal Crisis with Hyponatremia and Hyperkalemia
entities.description: Admission chemistry showing hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and depressed early morning serum cortisol indicating primary hypocortisolism from bilateral fungal adrenalitis.

entities.name: Absence of Historical Travel or Residential Exposure to Continental Latin America
entities.description: Complete lifetime absence of residence or travel in continental Latin America, which definitively excludes paracoccidioidomycosis as the environmental reservoir and endemic acquisition are strictly confined to this geography.

entities.name: Healthy Premenopausal Female Host with Normal Endogenous Estrogen Levels
entities.description: Presence of physiological circulating 17-beta-estradiol in premenopausal adult women, which potently inhibits the dimorphic transition from conidia to parasitic yeast, rendering chronic adult paracoccidioidomycosis exceptionally improbable.

entities.name: Absence of Multi-Budding Pilot Wheel Yeasts on Repeated Direct Microscopy of Mucosal Ulcer Scrapes
entities.description: Consistent failure to identify characteristic multi-budding mother yeasts on direct KOH smears or histopathology of active granulomatous lesions on repeated testing, strongly arguing against active disease.

entities.name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
entities.description: Mycobacterial infection presenting with chronic cough, hemoptysis, and weight loss, distinguished by apical and posterior upper-lobe cavitary consolidations, presence of acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear/GeneXpert, and absence of mulberry-like oral lesions.

entities.name: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
entities.description: Malignant epithelial oral neoplasm occurring in chronic smoking males, distinguished by indurated ulcers with everted hard borders and malignant cytology on biopsy, lacking moriform punctate hemorrhages and budding yeasts.

entities.name: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Protozoan infection caused by Leishmania braziliensis causing destructive mucosal ulceration in Latin America, distinguished by predominant cartilaginous nasal septal perforation (tapir nose), pulmonary sparing, and intracellular amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) within macrophages.

entities.name: Disseminated Histoplasmosis
entities.description: Endemic dimorphic mycosis caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, distinguished by tiny (2-4 μm) intracellular yeasts with narrow single budding within reticuloendothelial macrophages, contrasting with giant (15-30 μm) extracellular multi-budding pilot-wheel yeasts.

entities.name: Prolonged Oral Itraconazole Monotherapy
entities.description: First-line oral antifungal regimen (200 mg daily for 9 to 12 months) achieving >95% cure rate with low relapse in mild-to-moderate chronic paracoccidioidomycosis.

entities.name: Extended Oral Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole Regimen
entities.description: First-line alternative oral protocol (800/160 mg twice daily for 18 to 24 months) widely utilized in rural public health systems and effective for central nervous system disease.

entities.name: Intravenous Amphotericin B Deoxycholate or Liposomal Formulation
entities.description: Parenteral induction therapy (0.7-1.0 mg/kg/day conventional or 3-5 mg/kg/day liposomal) reserved for severe, life-threatening disseminated or respiratory paracoccidioidomycosis until stabilization.

entities.name: Hormonal Glucocorticoid and Mineralocorticoid Replacement Therapy
entities.description: Physiological replacement with oral Hydrocortisone and Fludrocortisone required to reverse refractory hypotension and electrolyte derangements in patients with Addisonian adrenal involvement.

entities.name: Complete Clinical Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial Agents
entities.description: Total failure to respond to empirical broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens (beta-lactams, macrolides, fluoroquinolones) for pulmonary infiltrates or oral ulcers, supporting a fungal rather than bacterial etiology.

relationships.target: Inhalation of Aerosolized Microconidia from Disturbed Acidic Soil in Latin America
relationships.keywords: respiratory transmission, inhaled microconidia, endemic soil
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Paracoccidioidomycosis is acquired via inhalation of aerosolized infective microconidia produced by saprophytic mycelia residing in acidic, humid soils of continental Latin America.

relationships.target: Rural Agricultural Worker in South America Coffee and Tobacco Plantations
relationships.keywords: occupational risk, manual agriculture, coffee crops, tobacco crops
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis develops with highest frequency following occupational exposure during manual soil tillage, coffee harvesting, and tobacco farming in rural South America.

relationships.target: Sylvatic Animal Reservoir Contact with Nine-Banded Armadillos and Rural Canines
relationships.keywords: zoonotic niche, sylvatic reservoir, Dasypus novemcinctus, rural dogs
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis shares an ecological niche with nine-banded armadillos (Dasypus novemcinctus) and domestic rural canines that serve as natural sylvatic and domestic reservoirs in endemic areas.

relationships.target: Male Agricultural Smoker with Chronic Alcohol Consumption Lifestyle
relationships.keywords: lifestyle risk, smoking habit, alcohol consumption, adult male predisposition
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis chronic adult form occurs overwhelmingly in adult male rural workers with heavy tobacco smoking habits (14-fold elevated risk) and regular intake of distilled spirits.

relationships.target: Absence of Inhibitory Circulating 17-Beta-Estradiol Protection in Adult Males
relationships.keywords: hormonal modulation, estrogen receptor, 17-beta-estradiol, male predilection
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis manifests with a 10:1 to 15:1 male-to-female ratio because physiological circulating 17-beta-estradiol in adult females binds to a cytoplasmic fungal receptor and blocks conidium-to-yeast transformation, a protection absent in post-pubertal males.

relationships.target: Prolonged Decade-Scale Clinical Latency Following Remote Latin American Residence
relationships.keywords: prolonged incubation, clinical latency, remote exposure, travel-acquired reactivation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis chronic form undergoes prolonged latency of 10 to 30 or more years, presenting as late reactivation long after leaving endemic Latin American rural regions.

relationships.target: Paracoccidioides brasiliensis
relationships.keywords: etiologic pathogen, dimorphic fungus, Ascomycota, species complex
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Paracoccidioidomycosis is caused by the thermally dimorphic fungus Paracoccidioides brasiliensis, which transforms from infectious environmental hyphae/conidia at 20-25°C into multi-budding parasitic yeast cells at 37°C.

relationships.target: Paracoccidioides lutzii
relationships.keywords: cryptic species, Center-West Brazil, Amazon basin, dimorphic yeast
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Paracoccidioidomycosis is caused by Paracoccidioides lutzii, a distinct molecular species prevalent in the Center-West and Amazon regions of Brazil displaying dimorphic multi-budding yeast morphology.

relationships.target: Moriform Painful Stomatitis with Mulberry-Like Granulomatous Gingival Ulcers
relationships.keywords: pathognomonic hallmark, Aguiar-Pupo stomatitis, moriform ulcers, mulberry appearance
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Paracoccidioidomycosis chronic form displays pathognomonic moriform stomatitis of Aguiar-Pupo in 50-70% of cases, consisting of painful granular mucosal ulcerations with pinpoint red hemorrhagic spots on gums, lips, and palate.

relationships.target: Acute Juvenile Fulminant Reticuloendothelial Dissemination with Suppurative Fistulizing Lymphadenopathy
relationships.keywords: juvenile form, suppurative lymphadenopathy, cutaneous fistulae, hepatosplenomegaly
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Paracoccidioidomycosis acute/subacute juvenile form presents in children and young adults with rapidly progressive massive lymphadenomegaly that softens, suppurates, and forms cutaneous draining fistulae, accompanied by marked hepatosplenomegaly.

relationships.target: Bilateral Adrenal Granulomatous Destruction with Primary Addisonian Adrenal Insufficiency
relationships.keywords: Addison syndrome, bilateral adrenal necrosis, melanoderma, postural hypotension
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Paracoccidioidomycosis chronic form causes bilateral adrenal granulomatous destruction in 15-50% of necropsies, manifesting clinically with asthenia, hypotension, skin hyperpigmentation, and adrenal crisis.

relationships.target: Chronic Progressive Fibrosing Pulmonary Syndrome with Exertional Dyspnea and Cor Pulmonale
relationships.keywords: respiratory syndrome, peribronchovascular fibrosis, cor pulmonale, exertional dyspnea
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Paracoccidioidomycosis chronic form causes progressive productive cough, dyspnea, and hemoptysis, driving extensive peribronchovascular fibrosis that progresses to pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale.

relationships.target: Microscopic Mariner Wheel or Pilot Wheel Multi-Budding Yeast on Direct KOH Preparation
relationships.keywords: direct microscopy, pilot wheel yeast, mariner wheel, Mickey Mouse head, KOH mount
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Paracoccidioidomycosis is diagnosed on bedside 10-20% KOH scraping by the pathognomonic pilot wheel (mariner's steering wheel / rueda de timón) yeast: a large 15-30 μm mother cell surrounded circumferentially by multiple narrow-necked daughter buds.

relationships.target: Bilateral Symmetrical Butterfly-Wing Infiltrates Spared at Apices and Bases on Chest Imaging
relationships.keywords: butterfly-wing infiltrates, bat-wing pattern, perihilar consolidation, apical sparing, reversed halo sign
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Paracoccidioidomycosis displays bilateral symmetrical reticulonodular and alveolar consolidations centered in the mid-lung and perihilar zones (bat-wing / butterfly-wing distribution) with characteristically spared lung apices and bases on chest radiography and CT.

relationships.target: High-Resolution CT Reversed Halo Sign with Perihilar Nodular Ground-Glass Opacities
relationships.keywords: reversed halo sign, atoll sign, ground-glass opacity, high-resolution CT
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Paracoccidioidomycosis high-resolution chest tomography demonstrates the reversed halo sign (atoll sign) characterized by central ground-glass opacity enveloped by a ring-like consolidation, along with parenchymal bands and centrolobular nodules.

relationships.target: Marked Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia Exceeding 10 to 30 Percent in Juvenile Presentation
relationships.keywords: peripheral eosinophilia, Th2 immune response, juvenile form, acute phase elevation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Paracoccidioidomycosis acute juvenile form exhibits marked peripheral blood eosinophilia (often 10-30% or higher) on admission CBC, driven by an aberrant Th2-skewed immune response.

relationships.target: Positive Serum Double Immunodiffusion Precipitin Band Against gp43 Antigen
relationships.keywords: gp43 serology, double immunodiffusion, precipitin band, diagnostic sensitivity
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Paracoccidioidomycosis exhibits high-titer precipitin bands against the Paracoccidioides brasiliensis gp43 glycoprotein antigen on quantitative double immunodiffusion with >90% sensitivity and >95% specificity.

relationships.target: Serum Electrolyte Pattern of Addisonian Adrenal Crisis with Hyponatremia and Hyperkalemia
relationships.keywords: hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, low morning cortisol, adrenal insufficiency labs
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Paracoccidioidomycosis with adrenal invasion exhibits admission laboratory derangements of hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia, and subnormal morning serum cortisol levels.

relationships.target: Absence of Historical Travel or Residential Exposure to Continental Latin America
relationships.keywords: geographic restriction, non-endemic exclusion, travel history
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Paracoccidioidomycosis is ruled out in patients who have never resided in or traveled to continental Latin America, as the environmental reservoir and endemic acquisition are strictly confined to this geography.

relationships.target: Healthy Premenopausal Female Host with Normal Endogenous Estrogen Levels
relationships.keywords: estrogen protection, premenopausal female, hormonal resistance
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Paracoccidioidomycosis chronic adult disease is ruled out with very high negative predictive value in immunocompetent premenopausal adult women due to 17-beta-estradiol inhibition of mycelial-to-yeast transformation.

relationships.target: Absence of Multi-Budding Pilot Wheel Yeasts on Repeated Direct Microscopy of Mucosal Ulcer Scrapes
relationships.keywords: negative direct microscopy, lack of pilot wheel yeasts, mucosal scraping exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Paracoccidioidomycosis is effectively ruled out when repeated direct KOH or calcofluor mounts of mucosal scrapings or exudates fail to show characteristic multi-budding mother yeasts in a patient with oral ulcers.

relationships.target: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, apical cavitation, acid-fast bacilli
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Paracoccidioidomycosis is differentiated from Pulmonary Tuberculosis by mid-lung butterfly-wing infiltrates with spared apices, moriform oral mucosal ulcers, and mariner's wheel budding yeasts, whereas Tuberculosis features upper-lobe apical cavitary lesions and acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear or GeneXpert.

relationships.target: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, oral malignancy, neoplastic ulcer, punch biopsy
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Paracoccidioidomycosis is differentiated from Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma by diffuse granular mucosal stomatitis with fine red hemorrhagic spots (moriform) and pilot-wheel yeasts that resolve with antifungal therapy, whereas Carcinoma exhibits solitary hard, everted margins with neoplastic epithelial cells on biopsy.

relationships.target: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, Leishmania braziliensis, tapir nose, Leishman-Donovan bodies
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Paracoccidioidomycosis is differentiated from Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis by pulmonary involvement, prominent gingival-palatal moriform ulcers, and large multi-budding yeasts, whereas Leishmaniasis selectively destroys the nasal cartilaginous septum (tapir nose), spares the lungs, and shows intracellular amastigotes within macrophages.

relationships.target: Disseminated Histoplasmosis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, Histoplasma capsulatum, intracellular yeast, narrow-base budding
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Paracoccidioidomycosis is differentiated from Disseminated Histoplasmosis by giant extracellular yeasts (15-30 μm) with multiple circumferential daughter buds, whereas Histoplasmosis exhibits tiny (2-4 μm) intracellular yeasts with single narrow-necked buds within macrophages.

relationships.target: Prolonged Oral Itraconazole Monotherapy
relationships.keywords: first-line therapy, oral triazole, clinical cure, maintenance regimen
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis responds rapidly and effectively to first-line oral Itraconazole (200 mg daily for 9 to 12 months), achieving >95% clinical cure rates and low relapse rates in mild-to-moderate disease.

relationships.target: Extended Oral Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole Regimen
relationships.keywords: alternative oral therapy, cotrimoxazole, CNS penetration, prolonged maintenance
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis responds to long-term oral Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (800/160 mg twice daily for 18 to 24 months), which is widely accessible in public health systems and provides excellent central nervous system penetration.

relationships.target: Intravenous Amphotericin B Deoxycholate or Liposomal Formulation
relationships.keywords: induction therapy, severe disease, polyene antifungal, liposomal amphotericin
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis severe or life-threatening disseminated forms respond to induction therapy with intravenous Amphotericin B (0.7-1.0 mg/kg/day conventional or 3-5 mg/kg/day liposomal) until clinical stabilization.

relationships.target: Hormonal Glucocorticoid and Mineralocorticoid Replacement Therapy
relationships.keywords: hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone, Addisonian crisis, adrenal replacement
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis-induced adrenal insufficiency responds to physiological hormone replacement with oral Hydrocortisone and Fludrocortisone, correcting hypotension and electrolyte disturbances.

relationships.target: Complete Clinical Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial Agents
relationships.keywords: antibacterial resistance, treatment failure, diagnostic verification
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Paracoccidioidomycosis is intrinsically resistant to broad-spectrum antibacterial agents (beta-lactams, macrolides, fluoroquinolones); lack of response in presumed bacterial pneumonia or stomatitis aids diagnostic recognition.
